title: Review bypassed Spring asynchronous advice
why: A direct same-class call bypasses the target method's requested asynchronous proxy advice, so that invocation does not gain asynchronous execution from the target annotation.
suggestion: When asynchronous dispatch is required, call a method on a separate managed bean or use an explicit asynchronous boundary.
limitations: Advisory, count-mode by default: method- or class-level canonical Async bindings use explicit imports, wildcard imports, or fully qualified names. Top-level nonabstract managed classes require canonical stereotypes or an unambiguous Bean return type. Direct same-owner calls provide structural evidence, not proof that asynchronous dispatch was intended.

Findings use the primary annotation location and group target calls in code_flow. Analysis abstains on extends/implements, same-name overloads, varargs or private/static targets, explicit generic receiver calls, other receivers, lambdas, and anonymous/local/inner classes.

Explicit per-module EnableAsync AspectJ mode suppresses this proxy-only rule. Dynamic configuration, custom meta-annotations, external type resolution, unresolved Maven properties or remote parents, and non-Java source are not resolved.
